title: Better line-of-sight checks, and honesty about the gaps
body: The terrain check now works out how much a hill actually blocks a radio path, using the standard diffraction maths and allowing for the curve of the earth, instead of a rough clearance score with hand-picked numbers. It also samples about twice as many points along each path while making fewer requests for height data. Where the height data does not cover a path, over open water or across the border, the tool now says it does not know rather than quietly scoring that path as average.

title: Says when a duplicate repeater was picked by guesswork
body: Two real repeaters can share the same 2-character prefix, and the tool has to pick one of them. Where there is a proven link it goes on that. Where there is not, it keeps whichever sits closest to the middle of the cluster, which is a guess, and a guess that pulls the estimate toward that middle. The cluster line now says how many prefixes were settled that way, so you can check those in the list below and swap the pick yourself.

title: Estimates no longer look more precise than they are
body: The estimated position was printed to five decimals, about a metre, while the search behind it works in squares of roughly 800 metres and testing against known positions puts the answer a median 2 km out. Coordinates are now shown to three decimals, and the tool says how far off it typically lands, so the result reads as an area to search rather than a doorstep.

title: Coverage now based on what a repeater can hear
body: A repeater's assumed coverage was built from every link it takes part in, including links only ever proven in the outbound direction. Those run much longer than links proven inbound, so coverage came out too generous. Where a repeater has enough inbound evidence the coverage is now based on that alone, and where it does not the tool says so rather than pretending. Antennas and receivers differ at each end of a link, so the two directions are not interchangeable.

title: Ignoring impossible repeater links
body: Each repeater's assumed coverage is worked out from the links it is known to have. Some of those links were hundreds of kilometres long, which no single hop can be at these radio settings, and that stretched a few repeaters' assumed range past 150 km. A repeater that wide stops helping narrow anything down. Links too long to be one hop are now left out, and the tool tells you how many it ignored.

title: Sharper estimates from overlapping observers
body: Observers are now combined by asking where all of them agree, rather than letting the loudest one outvote the rest. Estimates land about 16% closer in testing, and the heat map now shows where the answer is uncertain instead of looking the same everywhere.

title: Range and confidence outlines drawn correctly
body: The shaded outlines around proven-link ranges, clusters and the estimated area were collapsing to a line with no fill. They now show the real area they cover.

title: Repeater lookups working again
body: Searching by a 2-character prefix had stopped reaching MC Radar and was quietly falling back to a different dataset. It now uses the current API, and the app says so on the rare occasion it does have to fall back.

title: A short guide for newcomers
body: First-time visitors now get a walkthrough of the three steps and the tuning controls. Reopen it anytime with the ? button.

title: Share a link to your search
body: A Share button copies a link to your current clues, so you can hand someone the exact search instead of describing it.

title: Cleaner map controls
body: Buttons no longer float on top of the map. Clear Map and the 3D toggle now sit together above Step 1.

title: Shareable links
body: Step 1 can now be pre-filled from a URL, so other sites can link straight into a result instead of a blank form.

title: Smarter clustering
body: Repeaters heard through a relay (2nd-hop) are now included based on real network links where available, not just a flat guessed range.

title: Duplicate-node fix
body: Switching between duplicate nodes for the same prefix no longer silently resets the weight you'd set.

title: New top bar
body: Added a Dutch MeshCore-branded top bar with links to the community site, Mesh-Hunter, MC-Radar, and this project's GitHub.

title: Tighter default search radius
body: Cluster search radius now defaults to 6km instead of 50km, matching typical real-world repeater density.

title: Docker deploy
body: One-command deploy via Docker Compose with a built-in Cloudflare Tunnel sidecar.
